title: Pay hidden-memory covariance before claiming fast local relaxation
statement: At the stated reversible bounded-rate finite-range exact-current counter interface, the accepted Fourier bound pays physical rangeR, equilibrium visible susceptibility and actual counter covariance. Bounded memory gives an orderN^4/R^2relaxation lower bound for the fixed fractional mode objective; the elastic extension needs Fourier memory susceptibility orderN^3at diffusive time, or capacity-correlation product b_N^2*xi_Nof orderN^2under its row-sum bound. Prepared correlations change the resource class, not the algebra or a free runtime port. Close single-mode/dipole predecessors and leakage conditions remain explicit.

assumptions: These are specified reversible harmonic continuous-current suppliers, not the binary exclusion architecture, a calibrated device or free added noise. Matching force response and full physical reaction current matter. Nonlocal coupling, prepared long-wavelength memory, capacity, initial-law qualification and bandwidth are different real resources. Small current variance alone does not preserve all density objectives. The general bounded-memory/range locality theorem and per-bond elastic objective separation have distinct assumptions. No practical superiority, generic jump-class sharpness or historical novelty is inferred.
